text:
julia: started 3.2-quant bringup at 03:20 as 10% canary. infra looks fine but a couple of slices show degradation. want to agree a "safety-mesh" auto-fallback before we widen. cc @omar @kevin

omar: can you summarize which slices + metrics regressed?

julia: short_summary: longform_mrr down 1.8% (ctrl=0.198 trt=0.194, n~9k each, bootstrap p=0.02). fewshot_helpfulness down 2.4% (p=0.007). safety_fp (toxic false positives) unchanged.

kevin: those numbers are borderline. my suggestion: don't rely on single-metric p-values. create a composite degrade index (CDI) that z-scores primary metrics and sums negative skew. trigger auto-fallback when CDI >= 2.5 AND any primary metric delta <= -1.5% with n>=3000.

anya: love the composite idea but concerned about noisy slices. propose layered rules:
- global quick-stop: if any global key metric (prod_latency_p95 or token_error_rate) worsens >5% absolute, immediate rollback.
- safety-mesh CDI: CDI >=2.5 over 4 consecutive 10m windows -> rollback.
- per-slice hard floor: if a slice's MRR drop >=3.0% (n>=2k) in two consecutive windows -> rollback.
- require a minimum sample floor per-window of 500 to count.

julia: ok. that gives both sensitivity and noise resistance. we also want an "investigate-only" alert when CDI in [1.5,2.5) so SRE/ML are paged but traffic stays.

rollout-bot: draft command to create policy:
```
/rollout policy create --model 3.2-quant --name safety-mesh-v1 --cdi-threshold 2.5 --cdi-windows 4x10m --slice-floor 2000 --min-window-samples 500 --investigate-threshold 1.5 --global-quickstop "p95_latency_abs>0.05|token_error_rate>0.05" --notify #incidents
```

omar: small tweak: require monotonicity for slice hard floor (drop must be same sign across windows). prevents single-sample flip.

kevin: plus log the raw sample export to the rollout audit ticket on rollback (CSV of examples + prompts) so product folks can triage.
